intro: Follow a signal through the brain. Collect five discoveries to light up the station.
brainIntro: Scan three brain regions. Then use what you learned to solve three everyday clues.
neuronIntro: Help a neuron fire and find out how its message reaches the next cell.
reactionIntro: Wait for GO, then tap the beacon or press Space or Enter. See how three tries compare.
memoryIntro: Flip two specimen cards. Remember where each picture is hiding and match its twin.
quizIntro: Use clues from your missions to complete the final debrief.

regions.name: Cerebrum
regions.description: The large, wrinkled part helps you think, sense your surroundings, remember, and move on purpose. Many areas work together.

regions.name: Cerebellum
regions.description: The rounded part near the back helps fine-tune movements and balance, such as when you ride a bike.

regions.name: Brainstem
regions.description: This part connects the brain and spinal cord. It helps control automatic jobs such as breathing.

stages.name: Dendrites
stages.description: Branchlike dendrites receive messages from other cells.

stages.name: Cell body
stages.description: Incoming messages can make the neuron more or less likely to fire.

stages.name: Axon
stages.description: If the neuron fires, an electrical pulse travels along its axon.

stages.name: Synaptic terminals
stages.description: The pulse reaches axon endings, which can release chemical messengers.

stages.name: Synapse
stages.description: Chemical messengers cross a tiny gap and can change the activity of the next cell.

quiz.prompt: Which part helps you balance on a bike?
quiz.explanation: The cerebellum helps fine-tune movement and balance.

quiz.prompt: Where does an electrical pulse travel after a neuron fires?
quiz.explanation: The electrical pulse travels along the axon. Chemical messengers can then cross a gap.

quiz.prompt: What helps you hold a card’s location in mind for a few seconds?
quiz.explanation: Working memory holds and uses information briefly, such as a location you just saw.

quiz.prompt: What might change your reaction game score?
quiz.explanation: Attention and device timing can affect the result. This game is a demonstration.

quiz.prompt: You’re asleep. Which region helps keep you breathing?
quiz.explanation: The brainstem helps control automatic jobs such as breathing.

glossary.name: Neuron
glossary.description: A cell that receives and sends signals.

glossary.name: Synapse
glossary.description: A junction where a neuron passes a message to another cell.

glossary.name: Working memory
glossary.description: Holding and using information for a short time.

glossary.name: Cerebellum
glossary.description: A region that helps fine-tune movements and balance.

glossary.name: Action potential
glossary.description: A brief electrical pulse that can travel along a neuron’s axon.

glossary.name: Neurotransmitter
glossary.description: A chemical messenger that can carry a signal across a synapse.
